solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply 2x by both terms of the second bracket.
Multiply 3 by both terms of the second bracket.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second, collect like terms, and check the result for a common factor.

whyThisWorks.value: When both brackets carry coefficients, the leading term is the product of those coefficients times x², so 2x × 5x gives 10x². The two cross-products are still like terms and combine into a single x-term. The common factor of 5 appears because the second bracket, 5x − 5, is itself 5(x − 1), so the whole product had a factor of 5 built into it from the start.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the first term as 10x instead of 10x².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the first term as 10x instead of 10x².

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying only 2x × 5x and 3 × (−5) and missing the cross-terms.

commonErrors.misconception: Sign errors on −10x, giving +10x and hence a middle term of 25x.

examTip.value: Scan each bracket for a common factor before expanding. Taking the 5 out of (5x − 5) first turns this into 5(2x + 3)(x − 1), which is much quicker to expand.
